channel.description: Recent content in Writing on Best of AI

item.title: Constant Contact
item.description:
Constant Contact has been a staple of small business email marketing for a long time. Users build mailing lists, design emails from templates with a drag-and-drop editor, schedule campaigns, and track opens and clicks. It emphasizes ease of use and customer support, including phone and chat help, which appeals to owners who are not marketing specialists.

The product extends beyond email. Tools include SMS marketing, social media posting, landing pages, online surveys, and event registration, with automation for welcome series and follow-ups. AI features generate email copy and subject lines, suggest content ideas, and help build campaigns from a short brief, and an AI-driven website builder is part of the suite.

item.title: Squibler
item.description:
Squibler is a writing platform for longer projects. Authors plan a book with outlines and a corkboard, write in a distraction-free editor, and track characters, settings, and plot threads. An AI assistant generates outlines, suggests plot developments, and drafts text on request.

It targets novelists, nonfiction authors, and scriptwriters, with templates for different forms and export to formats ready for self-publishing. Collaboration features let editors comment.

Squibler has a free trial and paid plans. AI-drafted text should be edited heavily, and publishing platforms ask authors to disclose AI-generated content. Alternatives include Scrivener, Sudowrite, Atticus, Novelcrafter, and Google Docs. Squibler suits authors organizing long manuscripts.

item.title: Substack
item.description: Substack makes it simple to start a paid newsletter. A writer creates a publication, writes posts in an editor, and sends them to subscribers by email and on the web. The platform handles hosting, email delivery, and payments, so there is no technical setup. Writers can offer free and paid tiers, and subscribers pay monthly or annually, with Substack taking a percentage of paid subscriptions, in addition to payment processing fees.

item.title: academic-research-skills
item.description:
This repository bundles the following skills:

  • Deep Research: A 13-agent research skill with modes including full, quick, review, and fact-check.
  • Academic Paper: A 12-agent paper-writing skill with modes including plan, outline-only, and revision.
  • Academic Paper Reviewer: A 7-agent multi-perspective review skill with full and re-review modes.
  • Academic Pipeline: A 10-stage orchestrator skill managing the full workflow with integrity verification.

item.title: nature-skills
item.description:
This repository bundles the following skills:

  • nature-reader: Generates a bilingual Chinese-English Markdown reader of a paper with figure-text alignment.
  • nature-polishing: Revises academic text into Nature-style English with consistent terminology.
  • nature-paper2ppt: Converts a research paper into a presentation deck.
  • nature-reviewer: Simulates a blinded, three-reviewer peer review.
  • nature-response: Generates a point-by-point rebuttal to reviewer comments.
  • nature-figure: Produces publication-grade, multi-panel scientific figures.
  • nature-academic-search: Performs multi-source literature search with citation verification.

item.title: Paperpal
item.description:
Paperpal is designed for researchers. It works in a web editor, a Word add-in, and a browser extension, checking grammar, clarity, and tone against academic conventions. Suggestions are tuned to scholarly writing, where general tools may flag correct technical phrasing.

Beyond language editing, it offers help with paraphrasing, summarizing, and reference management, plus a literature search feature that finds papers and answers questions with citations. A journal submission check reviews manuscripts against common requirements before submission.

item.title: Trinka
item.description:
Trinka is built for scholarly and professional documents. It reviews text for grammar, style, and consistency with academic conventions, and understands field-specific terms in areas like medicine, engineering, and law. Suggestions explain why a change is recommended.

Extra tools check for plagiarism and consistency, offer paraphrasing, and run publication readiness checks. Plugins work with Microsoft Word and browsers, and a web editor is available.

Trinka has a free tier and paid plans. Authors should follow journal policies on AI-assisted editing. Alternatives include Paperpal, Grammarly, Writefull, Wordvice AI, and QuillBot. Trinka suits researchers and students polishing manuscripts.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5
item.description: Claude Sonnet 5 launched on June 30, 2026 as Anthropic’s most agentic Sonnet model yet, built to plan multi-step tasks and use tools like browsers and terminals with less hand-holding than earlier Sonnet versions. It performs close to Claude Opus 4.8 on most benchmarks, including roughly 85.2 percent on SWE-bench Verified and 63.2 percent on SWE-bench Pro, while costing noticeably less, which is why Anthropic and reviewers have framed it as a cheaper way to run coding agents at scale. It carries a 1 million token context window with context compaction to manage long agent sessions, and reads both text and images. Anthropic priced it at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through August 31, 2026, after which it moves to standard pricing of $3/$15, and it is now the default model for free and Pro Claude.ai plans.

item.title: ConvertKit
item.description:
ConvertKit was designed for independent creators rather than traditional businesses. It makes it easy to build a list with forms and landing pages, tag subscribers by interest, and send newsletters and automated sequences. The company later renamed the product Kit, and the old name remains widely used.

Creator commerce is a major part. Users can sell digital products, paid newsletters, and subscriptions directly, with payments handled in the platform. A recommendation network lets creators promote each other’s newsletters, and automations route subscribers based on what they click. AI tools help draft emails and subject lines.

item.title: Enhancv
item.description:
Enhancv guides people through writing a resume. A user chooses a template, fills in experience, and gets prompts and suggestions on wording, such as adding numbers to show results and avoiding vague phrases. A content analyzer scores the draft and points out weak areas.

Templates are designed to be readable by applicant tracking systems, and sections can be customized for different roles. Additional tools include cover letter help, a resume checker, and a personal website option. AI features suggest bullet points and rewrite text, which can save time when starting from scratch.

item.title: GetResponse
item.description:
GetResponse bundles several marketing tools. Users collect subscribers with forms and landing pages, send newsletters, and build automated workflows that respond to behavior such as signing up, clicking, or buying. A webinar feature lets businesses host live events and follow up with attendees.

AI helps create content. An assistant drafts emails, subject lines, and landing pages, and builds campaigns from a short brief, while segmentation and analytics help improve results. E-commerce features include product recommendations and abandoned cart emails, and integrations connect with online stores and CRMs.

item.title: Jobscan
item.description:
Jobscan helps people tailor resumes to individual jobs. A user pastes in a resume and a job posting, and Jobscan reports a match score, lists keywords and skills from the posting that are missing or underused, and points out formatting problems that could trip up automated parsers.

Additional tools include a LinkedIn optimization feature, cover letter checks, and AI that suggests wording and rewrites sections. A job tracker helps organize applications. The service is popular with career coaches and people applying to large companies that use applicant tracking systems.

item.title: Mailchimp
item.description:
Mailchimp is one of the best-known email marketing services. You build an audience list, design emails with a drag-and-drop editor or templates, and send campaigns with reporting on opens and clicks. Automations send welcome series, abandoned cart reminders, and birthday messages, and signup forms and landing pages help grow the list. It also supports basic CRM features, social posting, and simple websites.

AI is built into content and targeting. Generative tools help write subject lines and email text, and build designs from a brand’s assets. Predictive segmentation estimates customer behavior, such as likelihood to buy, and send-time optimization chooses delivery times. Intuit’s AI assistant brings help with questions about campaigns. Integrations connect with Shopify, WooCommerce, and hundreds of other apps.

item.title: MailerLite
item.description:
MailerLite offers the core tools of email marketing without clutter. Users build a list, design emails with a drag-and-drop editor, set up automations that respond to subscriber behavior, and publish landing pages and sign-up forms. Websites and simple stores can also be built within the platform.

Features include segmentation, A/B testing, an AI writing assistant, and e-commerce integrations with Shopify and WooCommerce. Analytics show opens, clicks, and revenue. Paid subscription newsletters are supported, which has drawn creators.

item.title: Warmbox
item.description:
Warmbox addresses a deliverability problem. New or little-used email accounts sending outreach often land in spam. Warmbox connects an account to a network of inboxes that exchange emails, open and reply to them, and gradually build a positive sending history.

It is used before and during cold email campaigns, with dashboards that show inbox placement and health. Settings control volume and ramp-up.

Warmbox is paid, with plans by mailboxes. Warm-up does not fix poor targeting or bad content, and spam laws still apply. Alternatives include Instantly, Smartlead, Lemwarm, Mailreach, and Warmup Inbox. Warmbox suits teams sending cold email.

item.title: Writecream
item.description:
Writecream offers many small tools in one place. Users generate cold emails with personalized openers based on a prospect’s profile, write blog posts and ad copy, create images, and clone voices or make avatar videos.

Its outreach features appeal to sales teams that want personalization at scale, such as icebreakers for LinkedIn or email. Other tools cover general content needs.

Writecream has a free tier and paid plans. Generic AI personalization can feel obvious to recipients, and outreach must follow spam and privacy law. Alternatives include Lemlist, Copy.ai, Jasper, Instantly, and Clay. Writecream suits small teams wanting varied content tools.

item.title: Writer
item.description:
Writer targets large organizations that need AI output to stay on brand and compliant. Teams set style guides, terminology, and rules, and the system applies them as people draft, with checks for claims and tone. A knowledge graph lets AI answer from company data.

The company builds its own Palmyra language models and a platform for building agents that handle multi-step work across tools. Governance features such as permissions, logging, and fact checks support regulated industries.

item.title: ActiveCampaign AI
item.description:
ActiveCampaign is built around automation. You design customer journeys that react to behavior: someone joins a list, visits a page, abandons a cart, or opens an email, and the system sends the right follow-up at the right time. Segmentation, split testing, site tracking, and a built-in CRM let small and mid-sized businesses personalize campaigns without a large marketing team. It is common in e-commerce, services, and B2B companies.

Its AI tools help build and manage those journeys. Active Intelligence can audit an account, draft campaigns and automations from a short description, flag automations that are broken or underperforming, and answer questions about results in plain language. Predictive features estimate the best time to send, how likely a contact is to buy, and which deals are most likely to close. A content assistant writes subject lines and email copy.

item.title: AI-Writer
item.description:
AI-Writer takes a different approach from many article generators. You provide a headline and optional keywords, and it creates a full-length article that pulls in information from sources it finds and cites them, so the draft includes references you can check. This responds to a common complaint about AI writing, which is that it makes claims without support.

Additional features support content marketing. It offers SEO analysis to guide the article toward relevant terms, a built-in indicator that shows how much of the text is verifiable against its sources, and tools for creating outlines, rewriting, and summarizing. The tool is aimed at bloggers, affiliate marketers, and agencies that publish many articles.

item.title: Anyword
item.description:
Anyword’s distinguishing feature is its performance prediction. When you ask for ad copy or an email subject line, the platform generates several versions and gives each a predicted score, based on models trained on large amounts of marketing performance data, along with an estimate for different audiences. The idea is to help marketers choose which copy to test or publish instead of guessing.

It works across typical marketing needs: ad copy for social and search, email campaigns, landing pages, blog content, and product descriptions. Brand voice settings and a knowledge base keep outputs consistent with a company’s tone and facts. Teams can integrate it with ad platforms and other tools, and an analytics layer connects the predictions with actual results. Targeting options adapt copy to specific audience segments.

item.title: Article Forge
item.description:
Article Forge is one of the older AI article generators. You enter a keyword and optionally subtopics, and it produces a long article with headings, sections, and optionally images and videos, in a few minutes. It was designed for people who publish a lot of content, such as affiliate sites, small business blogs, and agencies that manage many clients.

Further tools support publishing. A built-in scheduler can post articles to WordPress automatically, an uniqueness check helps avoid duplicate content, and options control article length, language, and tone. A rewriting function can adjust text, and API access lets developers integrate generation into other systems.

item.title: AutoCrit
item.description:
AutoCrit is an editing tool for novelists. A writer pastes in a chapter or uploads a manuscript, and the software reports on things editors look for: repeated words and phrases, adverbs, filter words, clichés, sentence variety, and dialogue. Reports highlight the text so you can see where to revise.

Its distinctive feature is comparison with published fiction. It measures a manuscript against patterns from successful books in the same genre, such as pacing and the balance of dialogue and description, so a writer can see how their draft differs. Generative features offer suggestions on revision and brainstorming, and a library of guides helps with craft.

item.title: Boomerang
item.description: Boomerang adds time management to Gmail and Outlook. You can write an email and schedule it to send later, set a message to return to your inbox if nobody replies by a certain date, or hide an email until the moment you want to deal with it. Recurring messages, read receipts, and a pause feature that holds incoming mail until you choose to see it help people manage busy inboxes.

item.title: Brevo AI
item.description:
Brevo started as an email marketing service called Sendinblue and has expanded into a broader customer engagement suite. It covers email and SMS campaigns, WhatsApp messaging, transactional email for apps, landing pages, forms, live chat, and a CRM for sales pipelines. Automation workflows send messages based on behavior, such as a signup or abandoned cart, and segmentation lets marketers target the right audience.

AI features support content and timing. A writing assistant drafts subject lines and email copy, generates images, and adjusts tone, while send-time optimization picks the best time to reach each contact. Predictive tools estimate engagement, and AI chat features help with customer conversations. The product is positioned for small and mid-sized businesses that want many channels in one tool at a reasonable price.

item.title: ChatGPT Canvas
item.description:
Canvas changes how you work with ChatGPT on longer projects. When a request involves writing a document or code, ChatGPT can open a separate pane next to the conversation, where the text or code appears as an editable file. You can edit it directly, highlight a passage and ask ChatGPT to change just that part, and see changes without the whole response being regenerated.

For writing, shortcuts adjust the length, reading level, and tone, add polish or emojis, and suggest edits inline like a collaborator leaving comments. For coding, Canvas helps review code, add comments and logs, fix bugs, and port a project to another language, and it can run some code, such as Python, within the interface. Version history lets you go back to earlier drafts.

item.title: Chibi AI
item.description:
Chibi AI aims to support writers who produce longer pieces. It provides a clean editor where you can draft with AI help, continue a passage, rewrite sections, and adjust tone or length, with a focus on staying in the flow of writing instead of juggling templates. The tool is aimed at bloggers, students, and fiction writers who want a collaborator that suggests next paragraphs or alternative phrasing.

It offers features common to AI writing tools, such as outline generation, summarizing, expanding ideas, and fixing grammar, with options to guide the style. Users can save projects and export their writing. The simple interface keeps focus on the text instead of a long menu of tools.

item.title: Compose AI
item.description:
Compose AI works wherever you type in Chrome. As you write an email or a message, it suggests the next words or sentence, which you accept with a keystroke, similar to code completion in a programming editor. It can also draft whole replies, rewrite text in a different tone, and fix grammar, with a menu of shortcuts for common tasks.

The product came from a startup that focused on autocomplete for writing, and later added generative features that call large language models for longer tasks. It is intended to save keystrokes on repetitive writing such as emails, support replies, and social posts, and to reduce the effort of starting a draft. A free tier covers basic use, with paid plans for more generations and features.

item.title: Content at Scale
item.description:
Content at Scale launched as a tool for generating complete blog posts. You enter a keyword, a URL, or a video, and the system researches the topic and writes a long article designed to read naturally, with sections, headings, and optimization for search. It was marketed on producing content that would pass AI detection and be useful to readers, which made it popular with SEO agencies and publishers.

The company has rebranded to BrandWell and widened its offering. It now describes a platform for brand growth that includes keyword research, content planning, optimization, and generation, with the long-form writer continuing as one of its core tools. Existing customers kept their accounts, and the older name may still appear on some pages or in billing.

item.title: Copy.ai
item.description:
Copy.ai began as one of the first popular AI copywriting tools. Users choose a template or write a prompt, and the tool generates headlines, product descriptions, email sequences, ads, and social captions. A brand voice feature helps keep the tone consistent.

The product later shifted toward workflows for go-to-market teams. Marketers and sales teams can chain steps that research accounts, draft outreach, and produce content at scale, using multiple language models. Chat and knowledge features let the AI draw on company information.

item.title: Copy.ai
item.description:
Copy.ai started in the first wave of AI writing tools. You picked a template, such as a product description, email, or social caption, answered a few prompts, and got several drafts to edit. It was popular with marketers and small businesses who needed a lot of copy quickly. Over time it moved away from one-off text generation and toward automating sales and marketing processes.

Its later product centered on workflows. A team could chain steps together, for example researching an account, pulling in data, drafting outreach, and writing a CRM update, and let AI agents run the sequence on a schedule or trigger. A data layer called Tables kept the inputs organized, and the aim was to replace manual go-to-market busywork with repeatable automations rather than just generating paragraphs.

item.title: Grammarly
item.description:
Grammarly started as a grammar checker and became the writing helper people keep installed everywhere. A browser extension, desktop app, mobile keyboard, and plugins for Word and Google Docs underline mistakes in emails, messages, and documents as you type. It catches typos and grammar errors, flags wordy or unclear sentences, and suggests a different tone, such as more confident or more friendly. A free version covers the basics.

Generative AI is built into the same flow. You can ask it to rewrite a paragraph, shorten a message, draft a reply to an email, or brainstorm ideas from a prompt. AI agents focus on particular jobs, such as giving feedback on a student paper, predicting how a reader might respond, or checking citations. Paid tiers add full-sentence rewrites, tone detection, plagiarism checking, and an AI detector, and business plans add style guides, brand tone, and analytics for teams.

item.title: Hypotenuse AI
item.description:
Hypotenuse AI is built for online stores with large catalogs. You upload a spreadsheet of products with attributes, and it writes descriptions for each one, in a consistent tone and optimized for search, saving the effort of writing hundreds or thousands of descriptions by hand. It can also produce category pages, meta descriptions, blog posts, and ad copy.

Features support brand and workflow. A brand voice setting keeps text aligned with a company’s style, a plagiarism check helps ensure uniqueness, and integrations connect with Shopify and other platforms to publish content directly. The product also offers AI image tools for creating and editing product images and backgrounds, which makes it a toolkit for content across a catalog.

item.title: INK Editor
item.description:
INK combines an editor with optimization guidance. As you write an article, the tool analyzes the search results for your target keyword and gives a score that reflects how well you cover the topic, which terms to include, and how readable the piece is. Suggestions appear in the sidebar, so you can improve the draft while writing instead of editing afterward.

AI features generate text and help overcome writer’s block. You can ask for outlines, introductions, and rewritten paragraphs, and use a plagiarism checker and content shield tools to monitor originality. The product works in a web editor and has extensions for common platforms, and teams can collaborate on content.

item.title: Jasper
item.description:
For copywriting, Jasper offers more structure than a general chatbot. Marketers choose a format such as a Facebook ad, a product description, a landing page section, or an email sequence, supply the details, and get multiple options in their brand’s voice. The Brand Voice feature learns tone and style from examples, and a company knowledge base provides facts about products and audiences so the copy uses accurate claims.

Collaboration features suit teams. Shared templates and style guides keep writers consistent, and campaigns can be planned in one place with copy, images, and variations for different channels. An editor helps refine text, change tone, and check for plagiarism. Newer agent features help automate common marketing tasks, such as producing a set of assets from a brief.

item.title: Jasper
item.description: Jasper was one of the first dedicated AI writing products and has focused on marketing teams that need a lot of on-brand content. You describe what you need, such as a product launch email or a set of ad variations, and it drafts the copy using your guidelines. Brand Voice learns your tone from sample content, and a knowledge base stores product details, audiences, and approved messaging, so output needs fewer corrections.

item.title: Jenni AI
item.description:
Jenni AI is designed around the way academics write. In its editor, you start a document and Jenni suggests how to continue sentences, offers to expand or rephrase text, and helps structure arguments. It can generate an outline from a topic and help draft sections, with the writer keeping control and deciding what to accept.

Research features distinguish it from general writing tools. You can search for academic sources, insert citations in styles such as APA and MLA, and manage a bibliography. A feature lets you upload PDFs and ask questions about them, so you can use sources more efficiently. The tool also supports different citation formats and exports to common document formats.

item.title: Kickresume
item.description:
Kickresume helps people create resumes quickly. You choose a template, enter your experience, and the builder arranges everything in a clean layout. A library of professionally designed templates covers different industries and styles, and the exports are designed to be readable by applicant tracking systems, which scan resumes before a human sees them. It also builds cover letters, personal websites, and portfolios.

AI assists with the writing. The AI resume writer can generate summaries and bullet points from your role and achievements, tailor a resume for a specific job description, and write a cover letter. A resume checker evaluates structure, keywords, and clarity and suggests improvements, and extra tools help with interview practice and job tracking. The AI features speed up drafting but can produce generic language.

item.title: Klaviyo AI
item.description:
Klaviyo is built on the idea that a store’s own customer data is the best basis for marketing. It connects to platforms like Shopify, BigCommerce, and WooCommerce, pulling in orders, browsing behavior, and product information. Marketers build segments, such as customers who bought twice in the last 60 days, and send targeted email and SMS campaigns and automated flows, like abandoned cart reminders, welcome series, and post-purchase follow-ups.

AI adds prediction and automation. Klaviyo estimates a customer’s likelihood to buy again, expected lifetime value, and probable next order date, and uses those signals for segmentation. Product recommendations personalize emails, send-time optimization chooses delivery times, and generative tools write subject lines and campaign copy and build flows from a description. A customer hub, reviews, and a CDP add other parts of the retention workflow.

item.title: Koala AI
item.description: Koala focuses on creating articles that are designed to rank. You enter a keyword, and the tool analyzes current search results, collects information from the web, and writes a structured article with headings, optional images, and links. It supports one-click generation of long pieces, and special modes for product reviews, listicles, and how-to guides. Real-time data is meant to keep information fresh compared with models that only use training data.

item.title: LanguageTool
item.description:
LanguageTool checks writing for spelling, grammar, punctuation, and style, and is notable for its broad language support, including English, German, French, Spanish, Dutch, Portuguese, and many more. It runs as browser extensions, add-ins for Microsoft Word and Google Docs, a desktop app, and an API, so it can check text wherever you write. Many people use it for writing in a second language or switching between languages.

The core engine is open source and can be self-hosted, which appeals to organizations with privacy requirements and to developers who want to integrate a checker. The premium tier adds more advanced style suggestions, tone and clarity feedback, and AI-powered rephrasing, along with higher character limits. Teams can set custom dictionaries and style rules.

item.title: Lex
item.description:
Lex is a document editor with AI woven in. The interface is clean and focused on writing, and the AI helps in small ways: continuing a thought when you are stuck, offering alternative phrasings, and giving feedback on drafts. Users keep control, and the tool tries not to replace their voice.

Features include a way to ask for critique, suggestions for headlines and next paragraphs, and the ability to have the AI respond to your own text in a side conversation. Writers use it for essays, newsletters, and notes where they want a thinking partner rather than automatic content.

item.title: LongShot AI
item.description:
LongShot AI is aimed at publishers and marketers who want blog posts with fewer unsupported claims. You provide a topic or keyword, and the tool researches the web and writes a structured article, with options to cite sources and run fact checks against search results. It can generate outlines, intros, and full drafts, and has a workspace for editing.

Additional features help with the content workflow. An SEO assistant suggests keywords and optimization steps, a rewrite tool paraphrases and adjusts tone, and a calendar helps plan publishing. Teams can collaborate in the editor, and templates cover common formats such as product reviews, how-to articles, and listicles. Users range from solo bloggers to small agencies.

item.title: Mixmax
item.description:
Mixmax turns Gmail into a sales workspace. It tracks opens, clicks, and replies, lets you schedule messages, and adds a calendar tool so recipients can book meetings from your email. Templates and snippets speed up repetitive writing, and polls, surveys, and documents can be embedded. It is used by sales, recruiting, and customer success teams that live in their inbox.

Sequences are a main feature: automated multi-step email campaigns that send follow-ups until someone replies, with rules for pausing and routing. Integrations connect with Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach alternatives, Slack, and Zapier, so activity is logged in the CRM. AI helps draft emails, personalize at scale, and suggest next steps, and call recording and meeting notes have been added in some plans.

item.title: Narrato
item.description:
Narrato helps teams manage the whole content process. A content calendar plans what to publish, assignments route work to writers and editors, and approval workflows track progress. The AI writer generates drafts, outlines, social posts, and ad copy in a team’s style, and SEO tools provide keyword suggestions and optimization scores.

Additional tools address agencies and publishers. Brief generation creates instructions for writers, a plagiarism checker and AI content detector help check originality, and a marketplace lets teams hire freelance writers for content that needs a human touch. Integrations publish directly to WordPress and other platforms, and an AI assistant helps with ideas and repurposing.

item.title: Originality.ai
item.description:
Originality.ai was built for people who commission or publish written content and want to know whether it was written by AI. You paste text or scan a URL, and it returns a score estimating the likelihood the text was generated by models such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, alongside a plagiarism check against web sources. Content teams, SEO agencies, and website buyers use it to check contractors’ work.

Additional tools include a fact-checking aid, a readability analysis, and a feature that shows the writing history of a Google Doc to demonstrate how it was composed. A Chrome extension and API support integration with publishing workflows, and team accounts allow reviewing many pieces. The company publishes accuracy studies, although its results are disputed by others.

item.title: Peppertype.ai
item.description:
Peppertype.ai started as a copywriting assistant and has grown into a broader content tool for marketers. Users pick a type of content, such as an ad, a product description, a blog outline, or a LinkedIn post, supply the topic and tone, and receive several drafts. Brand voice and knowledge settings help it reflect a company’s style, and templates cover many common marketing formats.

It is part of Pepper Content, a company that also runs a marketplace of freelance writers and managed content services, which is the source of the Peppertype name. That connection lets teams combine AI drafting with human writers and editors for higher-stakes content. Workflow tools support collaboration, review, and publishing, and the platform has added AI agents for tasks like research and repurposing content.

item.title: ProWritingAid
item.description:
ProWritingAid is built for writers who want to improve their craft. As well as catching spelling and grammar errors, it generates reports on overused words, sentence length variation, clichés, passive voice, pacing, dialogue, and readability, which editors and novelists use to revise drafts. The detailed feedback is aimed at long-form writing more than quick messages.

It offers integrations with Microsoft Word, Google Docs, Scrivener, and browsers, and includes a plagiarism checker in higher plans. Newer features use AI to rephrase sentences, suggest rewrites, and offer feedback on structure, and writers can set a house style or custom rules. A lifetime purchase option has been a distinguishing choice compared with subscription-only competitors.

item.title: Resume.io
item.description:
Resume.io helps job seekers create a polished resume quickly. You choose a template, fill in your experience, education, and skills in a guided form, and see the layout update. The templates are designed to be clean and readable by applicant tracking systems, and you can adjust colors and fonts, reorder sections, and download the result as a PDF. Cover letter and CV builders follow the same approach.

AI features help with the hard part, which is the wording. The assistant suggests bullet points for a job title, drafts a professional summary, and can tailor a resume to a job description. A resume checker highlights weaknesses, and a job tracker helps manage applications. The tool also provides guides and examples for different professions.

item.title: Rezi
item.description:
Rezi focuses on a specific worry: that automated screening software will reject a resume before a person reads it. The builder uses a simple, single-column layout and standard section names that parsing software reads reliably. As you write, a score shows how well the resume matches ATS best practices, with checks on length, formatting, action verbs, and keywords from a target job posting.

AI helps with content. It can generate bullet points from a role and tasks, rewrite weak phrases into stronger ones, and tailor a resume to a job description. It also drafts cover letters and has features for tracking applications and tuning your LinkedIn profile. The interface is plain, with less design flair than many competitors, which is intentional.

item.title: SaneBox
item.description:
SaneBox tackles inbox overload without replacing your email app. It connects to your existing account and analyzes your behavior, such as who you reply to and which messages you open, then moves less important mail into a folder called SaneLater. Newsletters, notifications, and cold outreach end up there, and you get a digest to skim when you choose. The important mail stays in your inbox.

Several tools help you stay in control. SaneBlackHole sends unwanted senders away permanently with a single drag, snooze folders let you hide a message until later, and reminders alert you if a recipient has not replied. A Do Not Disturb feature holds mail for a period. Because it works on the server, it functions with Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, Yahoo, and other providers, and on all your devices.

item.title: Sassbook AI
item.description:
Sassbook AI is a small suite of text tools. The AI story writer takes a premise and creates a narrative, with options to continue and steer the plot, aimed at hobby writers and students looking for ideas. Other tools summarize long text into shorter versions, paraphrase passages in different styles, and generate headlines and titles.

The tools work in a browser with a simple interface. Users paste text or enter a prompt, choose settings such as length or style, and get results they can edit. It also includes a plagiarism check and a few utilities for writers. The target audience includes bloggers, students, and casual writers who need quick help.

item.title: Scalenut
item.description:
Scalenut combines SEO research with AI writing. A user enters a keyword, and the platform analyzes search results to suggest topics, questions, and structure, then produces an outline and draft article, optimized for search. A one-click mode called Cruise creates a full article by following the steps of research, outline, and writing automatically.

Other features support content marketing. A keyword planner clusters terms into topics, an optimization score guides edits, and tools help with rewriting, product descriptions, and social content. The platform includes brand voice settings, a plagiarism checker, and a feature for tracking content performance. Teams can collaborate and manage projects in the app.

item.title: Scribbr
item.description:
Scribbr started as a proofreading and thesis editing service and built free tools for students. The citation generator formats references in common styles, the paraphraser rewrites text, and the grammar checker catches errors. A plagiarism checker compares text against sources, and an AI detector estimates machine-written text.

Students use these tools while writing essays and theses. Paid services include human editing by professional editors, which is a differentiator from purely automated tools. Guides explain academic writing topics.

item.title: Shortwave
item.description:
Shortwave is a Gmail client that rethinks the inbox. Related messages are grouped into threads, newsletters and receipts can be bundled so they do not clutter the main view, and snooze, scheduling, and split inboxes help you process email faster. It works on Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, and the web, and connects to your Gmail account.

AI is central. You can ask the assistant questions about your email, such as what a client asked for last month or when a trip was booked, and it searches and answers using your messages. It summarizes long threads, drafts replies in your tone, and can take actions like organizing, labeling, and scheduling. The goal is to cut the time spent finding and writing.

item.title: Spark Mail
item.description:
Spark is an email client that works with Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Yahoo, and other accounts. Its Smart Inbox sorts messages into categories, putting people and important mail first and keeping newsletters and notifications out of the way. Features such as snooze, send later, follow-up reminders, and quick replies make it faster to process mail, and a unified inbox combines accounts.

Collaboration is a differentiator. Teams can share emails, comment privately on messages, and draft replies together before sending, which suits small teams who handle shared mailboxes. AI features in the paid tier help write and rewrite emails, summarize long threads, and suggest replies, and a feature can search by asking questions. The app is available on Apple devices, Android, and Windows.

item.title: Superhuman
item.description:
Superhuman became known as the fastest email client. It’s designed so you can process your inbox with the keyboard, using commands for archiving, replying, snoozing, and reminders, and everything loads instantly. The interface is minimal, with Split Inbox sections that separate important mail from newsletters and notifications. Features such as send later, follow-up reminders, read statuses, and a command palette are built into the workflow.

AI is now part of the experience. It drafts replies in your voice, summarizes long threads, searches your mail in plain language, and can write emails from short prompts. The company that owns Superhuman acquired it, changed its own name to Superhuman, and groups it with Grammarly’s writing assistant and the Coda workspace in a combined suite.

item.title: Textio
item.description:
Textio focuses on how words affect people at work. Its model, trained on large amounts of text paired with outcomes like application rates, flags language in a job posting that may discourage certain candidates, such as gendered phrases or jargon, and suggests alternatives that attract a broader and larger pool. Recruiters get a score and specific edits as they write.

The platform extends to employee communications. Textio helps managers write clearer, fairer performance reviews and feedback by spotting vague, biased, or unhelpful phrases, and supports recruiting emails and other HR writing. Generative AI features help draft job posts and feedback from a few inputs while applying the same guidance. Integrations work within applicant tracking systems and email tools.

item.title: WordAI
item.description:
WordAI is an article rewriter. You paste in text, and the tool produces a reworded version that keeps the meaning but changes the sentences and structure. It was one of the earlier products built around natural language processing for this job, as opposed to older spinners that swapped in synonyms and produced awkward results.

People use it to adapt copy for different audiences, create alternate product descriptions, or refresh older posts. Settings control how much it changes, and you can review and edit the output. It sits alongside the Spin Rewriter and Chimp Rewriter type tools, and now competes with general AI assistants that can rewrite on request.

item.title: Wordsmith
item.description:
Wordsmith turns data into text. Users define templates and logic, connect a data source, and the platform writes a narrative for each record, such as a financial summary, a sports recap, or a personalized report. The output is consistent and can be produced in volume.

It predates today’s chat models. Rule-based natural language generation gives predictable text, which suits regulated reporting where exact control matters, while large language models offer flexibility and fluency but less predictability.

item.title: Writerly
item.description:
Writerly is aimed at teams that want AI-written content to sound like them. Instead of generating generic text, it lets users supply samples of their existing writing and style guidelines, then drafts articles, emails, and social posts that follow that voice. That approach is common among brand-focused writing tools, and matters most for companies with several writers.

Features reported in directories include templates for common content types, collaboration for editors and reviewers, and options to reuse past content. Teams often use this kind of tool to keep messaging consistent across channels and to speed up first drafts, with humans editing for accuracy and judgment.

item.title: Writesonic
item.description:
Writesonic started as a template-based copywriter and has widened into a content and marketing suite. Users pick a tool for blog articles, ad copy, product descriptions, emails, or social posts, give a brief, and get a draft. A long-form article writer can produce SEO-minded posts from a keyword with outlines and sources, and a chat assistant answers questions and drafts on demand.

Recent additions center on search visibility. Writesonic has tools to see how a brand is mentioned in AI answer engines such as ChatGPT and Perplexity, plus recommendations for improving content. It also offers brand voice settings, an editor with SEO scoring, and integrations with WordPress and other platforms.

item.title: Writesonic
item.description: Writesonic began as a template-driven AI writer for marketing copy. You choose a type of content, such as a blog post, ad, product description, or social caption, fill in some details, and get a draft. A longer-form article writer builds full posts with an outline, headings, and optional SEO guidance, and a chat assistant answers questions and can search the web. A browser extension and integrations with WordPress and other tools help get content published.

item.title: Zety
item.description: Zety walks job seekers through making a resume. You choose a template, answer prompts about your experience and education, and see a preview that updates as you type. The builder suggests wording for job duties and skills, which is helpful if you struggle with the phrasing, and it formats everything cleanly for PDF or Word download. It also builds cover letters and offers a library of guides and examples for different industries.

item.title: Beehiiv
item.description:
Beehiiv is built for people who run newsletters as a business. Writers compose and send posts, manage subscriber lists, and publish a website for the archive. Growth tools include referral programs, recommendations between newsletters, and landing pages, which help build an audience without outside ads.

Monetization is a central feature. Creators can sell paid subscriptions, run ads through the Beehiiv ad network, add sponsors, and offer digital products. Analytics show opens, clicks, and which posts convert readers. An AI assistant helps with drafts, subject lines, and ideas, and automation handles welcome sequences.

item.title: Copysmith
item.description:
Copysmith targets online retailers that need lots of product copy. A merchant can generate descriptions for many products from a spreadsheet or catalog, create ad headlines and text, and draft emails and social posts. Bulk generation saves time when a store has hundreds of items.

Integrations connect it to Shopify and Google Ads, so content can flow into the tools where it is used. Team features allow collaboration and approval, and brand settings keep tone consistent. Some tools support SEO optimization by suggesting keywords.

item.title: Ghost
item.description:
Ghost is a publishing tool focused on independent media. It provides a clean editor, a website with themes, email newsletters, and a membership system that lets readers subscribe for free or pay. Because it is open source, publishers can host it themselves or use Ghost’s managed service.

Business features are built in. Payments run through Stripe, so publishers keep most of the revenue, and analytics show how posts convert readers into members. The platform supports multiple tiers, comments, and integrations with other tools. A nonprofit organization develops it, which differs from venture-backed rivals.

item.title: HyperWrite
item.description:
HyperWrite started as a writing tool that predicted and completed text as you typed. It grew into a suite that includes a document editor, a browser extension that works across websites, and tools for rewriting, summarizing, and researching. Users can generate text from prompts and refine it in place.

The company has focused on agents. An assistant can navigate web pages, fill in forms, and complete multi-step tasks in the browser on a user’s behalf, which fits its idea of a personal AI assistant. It supports multiple underlying models.

item.title: Paragraph AI
item.description:
Paragraph AI brings AI writing to the smartphone. A user types a few words or dictates an idea, and the app produces a full email, message, or post, which can be adjusted for tone, length, or formality. Rewrite and proofreading tools tidy existing text.

The appeal is convenience for writing on the go, when opening a full desktop assistant is awkward. Typical uses include replying to emails, drafting social captions, and polishing short messages.

item.title: Shortly AI
item.description:
Shortly AI was one of the early GPT-based writing tools built for fiction and long-form content. A writer types, and with a keystroke the assistant continues the text in the same voice, or offers rewrites and alternatives. It aimed to keep the writer in control of the direction.

It was used for blog posts, stories, and essays, particularly to push through slow stretches. The product emerged before general chat assistants became widely used, and those assistants now cover much of the same ground.

item.title: Spike
item.description:
Spike presents email like a chat. Threads become conversations, which can feel faster, and a unified view combines email with notes, tasks, and calendar. Teams can discuss messages privately without forwarding.

AI helps with summaries of long threads, drafting replies, and organizing the inbox, and shared inboxes support small teams. It works with many email providers.

Spike has a free tier and paid plans. Chat-style email is a taste, and some prefer traditional layouts. Alternatives include Superhuman, Shortwave, Hey, Gmail with Gemini, and Front. Spike suits people who want a conversational inbox.

item.title: AIWriteBook
item.description:
AIWriteBook is aimed at people who want to produce a book without doing every step by hand. The workflow starts with a topic, generates an outline, drafts chapters, and offers editing passes. Extras include cover design and formatting for publishing platforms such as Amazon KDP.

Tools like this attract self-publishers, especially in nonfiction niches. They also raise concerns. Books produced mostly by AI can lack depth, accuracy, and a personal voice, and readers and platforms are wary of low-effort content. Amazon requires authors to disclose AI-generated content when publishing, and quality problems lead to poor reviews.

item.title: Automateed
item.description:
Automateed focuses on turning an idea into a finished ebook quickly. A user enters a topic or outline, the tool drafts chapters, and the author edits and arranges them. The platform then handles formatting and export in common ebook formats, with covers and other publishing steps in the workflow.

The audience is self-publishers and marketers who produce lead magnets, guides, and short nonfiction books. The convenience comes with tradeoffs. Mostly machine-written books can be generic, may contain factual errors, and face skepticism from readers and retail platforms. Amazon asks authors to disclose AI-generated content when publishing.

item.title: Bookbud
item.description:
BookBud.ai gives authors an AI workspace for book projects. A writer provides a premise or notes, and the tool proposes outlines and drafts sections of chapters, which the author reworks. The idea is to keep momentum when a blank page is the biggest obstacle.

Self-publishing authors use such tools to move faster, but quality depends on the human in charge. AI drafts tend toward the generic and can repeat or contradict themselves over a long manuscript. Readers value distinct voice and accuracy, and retail platforms ask authors to disclose AI-generated content.

item.title: Hemingway Editor
item.description: Hemingway Editor takes its name from the writer known for short sentences. You paste or write text, and the app colors problems: long, dense sentences in yellow and red, adverbs in blue, passive voice in green, and simpler alternatives for complicated words in purple. A grade level score estimates how hard the writing is to read, and the aim is to bring it to a level most readers can follow easily.

item.title: HumanizerFree.com
item.description:
HumanizerFree takes text produced by an AI model and rewrites it with varied phrasing, sentence length, and word choices so it reads less like machine output. A user pastes text, runs the tool, and edits the result. The tool is free for basic use.

Such tools raise questions. Using them to hide AI use in contexts where it is prohibited, such as some schoolwork, may break rules and can count as academic dishonesty. AI detectors are unreliable, so humanizers do not guarantee any result, and a rewrite can introduce errors or awkward phrasing.

item.title: NovelAI
item.description: NovelAI started as a tool for writers who wanted an AI collaborator for fiction. In its editor, you write a passage and the AI continues it, with controls for style, memory, and the characters and world in your story. Features such as lorebooks store details about characters and places so the AI keeps them consistent, and you can edit, retry, and steer the output freely. It’s used by hobbyist novelists, roleplayers, and fan fiction writers.

item.title: QuillBot
item.description:
QuillBot began as a paraphrasing tool and still draws most of its users for that. You paste in a passage, choose a mode such as standard, fluent, formal, or shorter, and it rewrites the text while keeping the meaning. A slider controls how much the wording changes. Students, non-native English speakers, and professional writers use it to rephrase awkward sentences, shorten drafts, and vary their style.

Around the paraphraser is a set of writing utilities. The grammar checker catches spelling and punctuation mistakes, the summarizer condenses long articles into key points or paragraphs, and the citation generator formats references in styles such as APA and MLA. A translator, an AI chat assistant, and detectors that estimate whether text is AI-written or plagiarized are included. Browser extensions and a Word add-in bring these tools into the places where people write.

item.title: Reztune
item.description:
Reztune helps job seekers customize applications. A user uploads a resume and pastes a job posting, and the AI rewrites sections to match the role, emphasizing relevant skills and adjusting wording to align with terms in the posting.

Tailoring takes time to do by hand, and tools like this make it faster, which appeals to people applying to many jobs. The risk is overstating experience or producing generic phrasing, so users should review every line for accuracy.

item.title: Rytr
item.description:
Rytr is a simple, affordable writing assistant. You pick a use case, such as a blog section, an ad, a job description, or an email, choose a tone, and give a short brief, and it generates a draft in seconds. It supports many languages and has built-in rewriting and expansion tools, plus a plagiarism checker in higher plans.

The editor resembles a text document, so you can generate content and edit it in one place. Rytr is used by freelancers, small businesses, and students who want quick drafts without learning complex tools, and its price is lower than many competitors. Chrome extensions and an API help use it elsewhere.

item.title: Sudowrite
item.description:
Sudowrite is designed for fiction writers. Instead of a generic chatbot, it provides tools shaped around storytelling: a Describe function that expands a moment with sensory detail, Rewrite options that change tone or style, Brainstorm tools for names, plot twists, and settings, and a feature to continue a scene in your voice. Writers can paste their own text and have the AI follow its style.

The platform has bigger story-level tools as well. Story Engine helps build a novel from a premise by generating characters, outlines, and chapters that the writer edits, and it keeps a database of story details so the AI maintains consistency. Sudowrite developed its own model focused on prose, and offers features for feedback and revision. It has appealed to authors who want a collaborator for drafting.

item.title: Wordtune
item.description: Wordtune is built around rewriting. Highlight a sentence in your draft and it offers several alternatives: shorter, longer, more casual, or more formal. You pick the one that sounds right and keep your own voice instead of pasting in a block of generated text. That makes it more of an editor’s tool than a text generator, which suits people who already know what they want to say and need help phrasing it.

item.title: WriteABookAI
item.description:
WriteABookAI helps authors move from idea to manuscript. A writer enters a premise, and the tool proposes an outline, character profiles, and chapter drafts, which can be edited. It aims at fiction and nonfiction, with tools to track plot and consistency.

Fully AI-drafted books tend to be generic and may contain errors or contradictions, and publishing platforms and readers expect disclosure of AI use. The best outcomes come from writers who use the tool as a drafting aid and add their own voice and expertise.
